interpretation.support_audit: Every dyad with non-zero published phenological overlap occurs as a positive interaction in at least one annual network; none of the 5,194 never-observed dyads has positive published overlap.
interpretation.primary_gain: Removing phenological_overlap reduces primary gain AUC from 0.8652 to 0.5142 and makes proper-score performance slightly worse than the null. The earlier strong gain predictive-filter interpretation is quarantined.
interpretation.primary_loss: Removing phenological_overlap leaves modest loss discrimination (AUC 0.5995; relative held-out log-loss reduction 0.0131), but the annual analysis remains retrospective and not causal.

not_a_claim_about_source_paper: This does not invalidate Peralta et al. (2020), which analyzed stability/functionality among observed interactions. It invalidates this project's reuse of the published overlap matrix as an outcome-independent predictor over the full candidate-dyad gain risk set.
required_next_step: Reconstruct an opportunity/phenology surface independently from raw dated visitor and flower-observation records with focal-response exclusion, then rerun the gain/loss audit.
claim_ceiling: Do not use the annual full-model gain skill or the zero-versus-positive phenology state pattern as evidence for ecological filtering, prospective forecasting, causal primacy, or routeability.
